item.title: Koshi Chief Minister Karki passes floor test

item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: Koshi Province Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki has won a vote of confidence.

A total of 57 members voted in favor of his motion of confidence at the meeting of the Koshi Provincial Assembly on Monday.

A majority of 47 is needed to form a government in the 93-member Koshi Province Assembly.

Karki, who represents CPN-UML, has the support of the Nepali Communist Party (NCP). UML has 40 members in the provincial assembly, while the NCP has 17.

The NC has 29 members in the provincial assembly. However, only 22 were present in the meeting on Monday. All of them voted against the motion.

Similarly, the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), which has five members including the Speaker, did not participate in the voting.

Janata Samajwadi Party (JSP) Nepal’s sole provincial assembly member, Nirmala Limbu, was absent.

item.title: Koshi Chief Minister Karki reshuffles cabinet, inducts NCP ministers
item.dc:creator: bishnu

Province Chief Parshuram Khapung appointed Khinu Langwa Limbu, Jeevan Acharya and Gombu Sherpa as ministers and Sapana Darji as minister of state on the recommendation of Chief Minister […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: Koshi Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki expanded his cabinet on Monday by inducting three ministers and one minister of state from the Nepali Communist Party (NCP).

Province Chief Parshuram Khapung appointed Khinu Langwa Limbu, Jeevan Acharya and Gombu Sherpa as ministers and Sapana Darji as minister of state on the recommendation of Chief Minister Karki on Monday. Khapung administered the oath of office and secrecy to the new ministers on Monday itself.

Chief Minister Karki, who represents the CPN-UML,  has also reshuffled his cabinet following the formation of a new ruling coalition with the NCP.  Indramani Parajuli has been given responsibility for the Ministry of Health, Bidur Kumar Lingthep for the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Planning, and Ram Prasad Mahato for the Ministry of Industry, Agriculture and Cooperatives.

Similarly, Tilchan Pathak has been assigned the Ministry of Water Supply, Irrigation and Energy; Khinu Langwa Limbu the Ministry of Tourism, Forests and Environment; Jeevan Acharya the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development; Gombu Sherpa the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Law; and Geeta Timsina the Ministry of Social Development.

Sapana Pariyar has been appointed as Minister of State for Physical Infrastructure Development, while Umakanta Gautam has been assigned the responsibility of Minister of State for Health.

item.title: Dharan endorses Rs 2.76 billion spending plan for 2026/27
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: ITAHARI: Following nearly a month and a half of deadlock caused by a dispute between the acting mayor and ward chairpersons, the budget of Dharan Sub-metropolitan City for the fiscal year 2026/27 has finally been approved. A meeting of the municipal assembly held on Thursday endorsed a spending plan of Rs 2.76 billion for the […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: Following nearly a month and a half of deadlock caused by a dispute between the acting mayor and ward chairpersons, the budget of Dharan Sub-metropolitan City for the fiscal year 2026/27 has finally been approved.

A meeting of the municipal assembly held on Thursday endorsed a spending plan of Rs 2.76 billion for the current fiscal year, which began on July 17.

The annual budget represents an increase of Rs 511.14 million compared to the previous fiscal year’s outlay of Rs 2.24 billion.

The budget-making process in the sub-metropolis had stalled earlier due to a feud between Acting Mayor Aindra Bikram Begha and several ward chairs over allocation of funds for troubled local cooperatives. The impasse cleared after both sides issued self-criticisms and agreed on shared priorities.

The new budget has named urban infrastructure, education, health, drinking water, cooperative management and social development as main priority sectors. The sub-metropolis has allocated Rs 50 million specifically under the economic development heading to address crisis-ridden financial cooperatives. Overall, Rs 680 million has been earmarked for the economic development sector to fund various programs in agriculture, livestock, tourism, industry, enterprise and local employment generation.

To resolve Dharan’s long-standing water scarcity, the sub-metropolis has set aside Rs 31.1 million as a cost-sharing contribution toward the federal government’s project to supply water from the Koshi River.

Similarly, Rs 995 million has been set aside for urban planning and physical infrastructure. Planned works under this allocation include a pothole-free city initiative, the beautification of Bhanu Chowk alongside the construction of a permanent stage, and the construction of the Dharan City Hall.

The budget has allocated Rs 498.68 million for the education, youth and sports sector. The amount also includes conditional grants received from both federal and provincial governments.

Additionally, the health sector has received Rs 124.5 million. The fund includes Rs 20 million for the operation of Dharan Hospital and Rs 5 million to implement programs in collaboration with the BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences.

The sub-metropolis has allocated Rs 260 million across its 20 wards to cover administrative, capital and program expenses. This marks an increase of Rs 50 million compared to the previous fiscal year.

Revenue Sources

To fund its expenses, the sub-metropolitan city aims to raise Rs 1.40 billion through internal revenue generation.

Similarly, it expects to receive Rs 861.9 million from federal government grants, Rs 91.64 million from provincial government grants, Rs 328.89 million from revenue sharing and Rs 10 million from the Road Board.

It plans to carry over Rs 70 million from the previous year’s cash balance.

item.title: NC ministers in Koshi submit their resignations
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: ITAHARI: Ministers representing the Nepali Congress (NC) in the Koshi Provincial Government have submitted their resignations. NC ministers submitted their resignations to Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki on Wednesday. The ministers tendered their resignations as per the party’s decision to end its alliance with the CPN-UML. The resigning cabinet members include Minister for Physical Infrastructure […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: Ministers representing the Nepali Congress (NC) in the Koshi Provincial Government have submitted their resignations.

NC ministers submitted their resignations to Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki on Wednesday.

The ministers tendered their resignations as per the party’s decision to end its alliance with the CPN-UML.

The resigning cabinet members include Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development Pradeep Sunuwar, Minister for Health Man Bahadur Limbu, Minister for Industry, Agriculture and Cooperatives Israil Mansuri, Minister for Tourism, Forest and Environment Bhim Parajuli, and Minister of State for Physical Infrastructure Development Shobha Chemjong.

After the NC decided to end its partnership with UML at the provincial level, UML has formed a new alliance with the Nepali Communist Party (NCP). As per the power-sharing understanding between the two parties, UML will continue to retain the leadership of the provincial government.
The resignation of NC ministers has paved the way for the NCP to join the provincial government.

The ruling party, however, has struggled to reach an internal consensus regarding who will hold the chief minister’s post. Party sources indicate that UML Chairperson KP Sharma Oli is in favor of appointing Til Kumar Meyangbo to lead the provincial administration.

However, incumbent Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki has reportedly insisted that he will step down only after a formal decision is made by the party’s Secretariat.

item.title: Internal dispute in UML delays government formation in Koshi
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The process of forming a new government in Koshi Province has been delayed due to a dispute within the CPN-UML over the chief ministerial candidate. As per a power-sharing deal between the UML and the Nepal Communist Party (NCP), the UML will form governments in Koshi, Bagmati and Lumbini provinces. Similarly, NCP will lead […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The process of forming a new government in Koshi Province has been delayed due to a dispute within the CPN-UML over the chief ministerial candidate.

As per a power-sharing deal between the UML and the Nepal Communist Party (NCP), the UML will form governments in Koshi, Bagmati and Lumbini provinces. Similarly, NCP will lead governments in Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces.

However, UML leaders are divided over whether to continue with incumbent Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki or bring in a new face. UML Chairperson KP Sharma Oli reportedly wants a new face to lead the provincial government.

Meanwhile, the Koshi Province committee of UML has begun consultations with provincial assembly members regarding government formation.

Sherdhan Rai, Koshi Province In-charge of CPN-UML, said the dispute over leadership would be resolved within one and a half weeks. He added that discussions have begun within both the party and its parliamentary wing to ensure implementation of party Chairperson Oli’s directives.

Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki said while he is not the only option to lead the province government, he is committed to uniting the party in the current context. He said that any discussion on government formation should also consider that the current government was formed under Article 168 (5) of the Constitution of Nepal, 2015.

According to provincial assembly member Panchakarna Rai, 29 UML lawmakers participated in the recent discussion on government formation

The CPN-UML has 40 members in the provincial assembly, including the deputy speaker.

item.title: Families of Dewangunj victims, govt sign seven-point agreement
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The families of two youths who were killed in police firing in Dewangunj, Sunsari, on Sunday night have agreed to receive and cremate the bodies after signing a seven-point agreement with the government. The agreement was signed on Friday morning by Minister for Home Affairs Sudhan Gurung and representatives of the victims’ families. Om […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The families of two youths who were killed in police firing in Dewangunj, Sunsari, on Sunday night have agreed to receive and cremate the bodies after signing a seven-point agreement with the government.

The agreement was signed on Friday morning by Minister for Home Affairs Sudhan Gurung and representatives of the victims’ families.

Om Prakash Mehta and Jaya Prakash Mehta died when police opened fire to control a clash between two communities in Kaptangunj of Dewanguj Rural Municipality of Sunsari on Sunday night. Om Prakash died while undergoing treatment on Sunday itself, while Jaya Prakash was declared dead on Thursday.

According to the agreement, the government will immediately initiate the process of declaring both deceased as martyrs. It has also committed to providing financial relief of Rs 1 million each to the bereaved families.

Similarly, the government has expressed commitment to conduct a fair and effective investigation into the incident and to iniate legal action against those found responsible as per the prevailing laws.

The government has agreed to launch a separate investigation into the legal status and related matters concerning a madrasa located in Dewangunj-3.

As part of the agreement, one qualified member from each victim’s family will be provided with employment opportunities.

The government has also expressed commitment to implement the recommendations of the investigation committee formed to study the incident.

Likewise, the agreement states that a memorial park will be constructed at a suitable location within the rural municipality in coordination with the local government.

item.title: Koshi announces relief package for Sunsari incident victims
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: ITAHARI: The Koshi Province Government has announced a relief package for victims of the recent violence in Dewanganj Rural Municipality of Sunsari. The province government has decided to provide Rs 200,000 to the family of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each to those injured as well as those whose homes, shops or other property were […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: The Koshi Province Government has announced a relief package for victims of the recent violence in Dewanganj Rural Municipality of Sunsari.

The province government has decided to provide Rs 200,000 to the family of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each to those injured as well as those whose homes, shops or other property were damaged in arson attacks.

Chief Minister Hikmar Kumar Karki made the announcement during an all-party meeting held in Biratnagar on Wednesday.

The meeting also adopted an eight-point resolution aimed at restoring social harmony and maintaining law and order in the province.

The participants of the meeting paid tribute to Om Prakash Mehta, who was killed in the incident, and extended condolences to his bereaved family. They also wished for the speedy recovery of the injured.

The meeting decided that political parties, social organizations and the administration would work to preserve social harmony and communal unity. It also decided to hold all-party and all-stakeholder meetings at the local level and implement programs to promote communal harmony.

To strengthen reconciliation at the community level, the provincial government has decided to work in coordination with local administrations to organize goodwill rallies and similar initiatives.

The meeting also decided that organizations representing all religious communities should issue a joint appeal requesting the public to maintain social harmony. It also called for heightened security vigilance against any undesirable activities that could originate from the border areas and urged the federal government to provide treatment support for the injured and relief assistance to the families of those killed.

The meeting also instructed the concerned District Administration Offices to coordinate with security agencies to strengthen security arrangements in the affected district and surrounding areas to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

Addressing the meeting, Chief Minister Karki urged all stakeholders to play their part in preserving social harmony and appealed to everyone to refrain from activities that could undermine communal peace during the sensitive period.

Rastriya Swatantra Party Koshi Province Chairperson Chandra Bahadur Rai, Nepali Congress Koshi Province President Uddhav Thapa, CPN-UML Koshi Province Chairperson Ghanshyam Khatiwada, representatives of various political parties, heads of provincial security agencies, and senior government officials, among others, attended the meeting.

item.dc:creator: bishnu

According to a notice issued by Chief District Officer Ishwori Prasad Aryal, the curfew has been lifted effective from 12:15 am on Tuesday. The order had been enforced from the border […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: The District Administration Office, Sunsari, has lifted the indefinite curfew imposed in different parts of Sunsari following Sunday night’s fatal incident in Kaptangunj.

According to a notice issued by Chief District Officer Ishwori Prasad Aryal, the curfew has been lifted effective from 12:15 am on Tuesday.

The order had been enforced from the border of Inaruwa Municipality–3 and 6 (Ghopali Tole) to the Koshi Barrage bridge, and within a 200-meter area north and south of the East-West Highway.

Earlier, the administration had imposed an indefinite curfew in the area from 9:00 pm on Monday until further notice.

The local administration said the curfew was lifted after reviewing the security situation. However, it added that prohibitory orders previously enforced in some sensitive areas of the district will remain in place.

One person was killed and 22 others were injured when police opened fire to take the situation under control after people of two communities clashed in Kaptangunj of Devangunj Rural Municipality.

item.title: Sunsari CDO, heads of security agencies recalled after Kaptangunj incident
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Ministry of Home Affairs has recalled Sunsari Chief District Officer (CDO) Basudev Ghimire and the heads of security agencies in the district following Sunday night’s deadly incident. Ghimire has been recalled to the ministry and replaced by Ishwari Prasad Aryal, the Chief District Officer of Sankhuwasabha. Similarly, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Binod Ghimire, […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Ministry of Home Affairs has recalled Sunsari Chief District Officer (CDO) Basudev Ghimire and the heads of security agencies in the district following Sunday night’s deadly incident.

Ghimire has been recalled to the ministry and replaced by Ishwari Prasad Aryal, the Chief District Officer of Sankhuwasabha.

Similarly, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Binod Ghimire, the chief of the Koshi Province Police Office, has been recalled to the Nepal Police Headquarters. DIG Shekhar Khanal has been posted to lead the provincial police office.

Similarly, SP Keshav Thebe, chief of the District Police Office, Sunsari, has been transferred to Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa. He will be replaced by SP Pushparaj Malla, who had been serving at the airport.

The ministry has also recalled Armed Police Force (APF) Nepal SP Shyam Kumar Karki and replaced him with SP Laba Kumar Sapkota from APF Headquarters.

Likewise, APF Nepal DSP Nanda Kishore Mahato, who was stationed in Kaptanganj, has also been recalled. DSP Madan Nath from APF Headquarters has been assigned to replace him.

One person was killed and 22 others were injured when police opened fire to control clashes between two communities in Kaptangunj of Devangunj Rural Municipality-3 of Sunsari on Sunday night.

Ten Nepal Police and five APF Nepal personnel were also injured in the incident.

The ministry has already formed a five-member probe committee, led by Joint Secretary Bhupendra Thapa, to investigate the incident. The committee has been given one week to submit its report.

item.title: Kaptangunj firing: Local government declares two days of mourning
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: ITAHARI: Devanganj Rural Municipality in Sunsari has declared two days of mourning after a man died from police gunfire during a clash between two groups on Sunday night. The rural municipality announced a two-day mourning period on Monday and Tuesday, expressing grief over the incident that occurred at Kaptanganj market area in Ward-3. Police say […]
item.content:encoded:
ITAHARI: Devanganj Rural Municipality in Sunsari has declared two days of mourning after a man died from police gunfire during a clash between two groups on Sunday night.

The rural municipality announced a two-day mourning period on Monday and Tuesday, expressing grief over the incident that occurred at Kaptanganj market area in Ward-3.

Police say they had to open fire to bring the clash between two communities under control. One person was killed and 22 others, including police personnel, were injured in the incident.

The deceased has been identified as Om Prakash Mehta (24) of Kaptanganj in Devanganj-3. He succumbed to gunshot injuries while undergoing treatment.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Home Affairs has formed a five-member committee to investigate the incident.
